audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL logic: transaction initcode validation (EIP-3860), EVM bitwise operations, JSON-RPC service discovery (EIP-1901), wallet provider injection security (EIP-5593), and byte utility functions.

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component calling byte utilities — not an external entity, resides within the EL system boundary
Internal function calling byte utilities — not an external entity, resides within the EL system boundary
The JSON-RPC service is the EL node itself providing RPC methods — this is the target component, not an external entity

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit contract creation transactions via public JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Initcode content is fully attacker-controlled.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Actor via Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker submitting large initcode to trigger expensive jumpdest analysis. Fully untrusted — no authentication, malicious intent assumed.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Client via rpc.discover
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any external client can call rpc.discover. No authentication required. Could be used for reconnaissance or to probe available methods.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Caller via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC 2.0 interface (any method including rpc.* namespace)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any external entity can make JSON-RPC calls. Unauthenticated public interface. Method names and parameters are attacker-controlled.

trusted_external_entities.name: Website/DApp via window.ethereum
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Websites request Ethereum provider access. Fully untrusted — any website can attempt to interact with the provider. Secure context checks gate access.

trusted_external_entities.name: Third-Party Iframe via window.ethereum
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Third-party iframes (ads, embeds) attempting provider access. Blocked by default. Fully untrusted — potentially malicious.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: initcode size must be checked against MAX_INITCODE_SIZE (49152 bytes), intrinsic gas must include initcode cost, gas limit must cover total intrinsic gas.
Initcode size limit enforced before expensive jumpdest analysis. Gas metering (2 gas/word) must cover computational cost. Size limit (49152 bytes) bounds worst-case analysis cost.
Service must not expose sensitive internal information via OpenRPC document. Rate limiting recommended. Response must be well-formed JSON-RPC.
All method names and parameters must be validated. Reserved rpc.* namespace must be enforced. Unknown methods must return proper error responses.
Secure context (HTTPS or trustworthy origin) must be verified before provider injection. window.isSecureContext must be true. Origin trustworthiness must be validated per W3C Secure Contexts spec.
Third-party iframes must be blocked by default. Cross-origin iframe must not receive provider unless explicit Permissions API grant. Sandbox attributes must be checked for first-party iframes.
